reason: The cited evidence does not support the key premises. E1 and E2 discuss an information-theoretic entropy method for solids, not ML potentials or liquid-phase free energies. E3 only states that ML is emerging for HEA screening and that high-quality datasets are a challenge, without demonstrating that ML potentials can capture anharmonic/electron-vibration effects or achieve the claimed speed/accuracy for fusion properties. The premises thus lack specific prior evidence.
premises: ML potentials can be trained to reproduce ab initio free energies for solid and liquid phases of a HEA
Targeted training data can capture anharmonic and electron-vibration coupling effects
The approach will yield 10-100x speed-up over explicit AIMD and TOR-TILD
The method is valid for CoCrFeNi near 0.9-1.1 Tm
